findings.summary: Bitcoin is a decentralized digital cryptocurrency introduced in 2009. It operates via a peer-to-peer network of computers (nodes) that each maintain an independent copy of a public distributed ledger called a blockchain. Transactions are validated using cryptography to prevent double-spending, and consensus on the ledger is achieved through a computationally intensive proof-of-work process known as mining, performed by specialized hardware. New bitcoins are issued according to a decentralized schedule, with block rewards halving approximately every four years, capped at 21 million units.

mechanisms.title: Transaction validation and double-spending prevention
mechanisms.explanation: Each node independently verifies transactions using cryptographic techniques. This ensures that a bitcoin cannot be spent twice, provided the owner keeps sensitive data secret.

mechanisms.title: Consensus via proof-of-work mining
mechanisms.explanation: Nodes reach agreement on blockchain content through a computationally intensive process called mining. Miners solve partial hash inversions using purpose-built hardware, securing the network and earning block rewards.
